jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral fellow in the role of 3D genome organization in obesity
jobs.description:
About the position / About the job
Applications are invited for a 4-year position as postdoctoral researcher in epigenetics and obesity research at the newly established K.G Jebsen Centre of Obesity ReseArch (CORA).

The position will be affiliated to Anita Göndör’s research group at the Department of Clinical Molecular Biology (EpiGen) at Institute of Clinical Medicine, UiO, physically located at Campus Ahus (Akershus University Hospital) (https://www.med.uio.no/klinmed/english/people/aca/anitagon/)

The project aims at exploring novel, transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms of gene regulation that govern adipose stem cell properties, preadipocyte expansion and differentiation for lipid storage in physiological and pathological conditions. 

 

 
 
The applicant will analyze the role of 3D genome organization in the regulation of human body weight and adipose tissue biology in general. Specifically, the tasks include the quantitation of super-enhancer-mediated gene gating to nuclear pores for gene regulation in different stages of adipocyte differentiation in vitro and ex vivo, in patient-derived tissues. We are looking for a candidate with extensive hands-on training on in situ and bulk assays designed to quantitate 3D chromatin states, gene expression variation, epigenomics, RNA biology and experience in work with small input material. The applicant will join a team with long-standing experience in investigating the role of nuclear architecture and chromatin organization in development and disease, while other research groups in the department are working on translational biomedical research focusing on Alzheimer´s, obesity, bioinformatics and molecular biology-based cancer research, with a focus on precision medicine.

 
Project description
The project is part of a newly established K.G. Jebsen Center for obesity research (CORA, https://stiftkgj.no/en/senter/k-g-jebsen-center-for-obesity_research/), which aims at i) understanding the biological mechanisms underlying weight regain after weight loss, ii) identifying individuals at risk, and iii) developing strategies for sustained weight loss and long-term weight maintenance.

Anita Göndör`s research group is a participant in the center aiming at investigating the role of novel gene regulatory mechanisms that control the expansion of preadipocytes as well as the perturbation of these processes on the path to obesity. In CORA, the group will specifically focus on the role of 3D genome organization in adipose tissue and its role in wight re-gain after weight loss. The candidate will be closely involved in interdisciplinary collaborations with molecular biologists focusing on epigenetic mechanisms in obesity and clinical environments in Norway and abroad.

jobs.description:
The position
Do you want to contribute to research about non-coding RNAs in sperm health and infertility?

A PhD position is available at the Department of Clinical Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences in the Translational Vascular Research group, working on the project ´Developmental non-coding RNA signatures of sperm health and infertility´

The Translational Vascular Research group includes both basic scientists and clinicians. We perform research spanning across disciplines, from the analysis of patient samples to laboratory based investigation of cell behaviour. Parts of our research group are based at Karolinska Institute/KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden, with the opportunity for close collaborations with these institutes.The fertility department at the Women’s clinic at the University Hospital of North Norway (UNN) is a collaboration partner and will contribute with expertise in andrology and analysis of semen samples.

The position is for a period of four years. The nominal length of the PhD program is three years. The fourth year is distributed as 25% each year and will consist of teaching and other duties for the Department of Clinical Medicine. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to a PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position. 

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.
The project 
Male infertility is an increasing global health concern, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired sperm function remain poorly understood. Previously, our group identified more than 2,000 testis-enriched non-coding RNAs and characterised their expression across germ-cell development. In this project, you will investigate which of these non-coding RNAs persist into mature sperm and whether their expression is associated with sperm quality and fertility. In collaboration with the fertility clinic atthe University Hospital of North Norway (UNN), you will analyse sperm samples from fertility patients and healthy donors. Using sperm phenotyping, cell sorting and RNA sequencing, you will examine differences in non-coding RNA expression between sperm populations with different functional characteristics, including motility and morphology. Selected transcripts will also be investigated in matched testicular tissue using imaging and in situ hybridisation to study their expression during germcell development. By integrating molecular and clinical data, the project aims to identify non-coding RNA signatures associated with sperm health and their potential as biomarkers of male fertility.
 
You must submit a cover letter explaining your motivation and research interests.

The PHASE Group at the Department of Chemical Engineering at NTNU has a vacant PhD position in which experimental techniques in microfluidics and lab-scale flotation will be used to investigate the recovery of solid mineral particles via bubble formation. The work is part of the project MINBUBBLE funded by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation. The PhD candidate will collaborate with researchers within the PHASE group and at KTH Royal Institute of Technology who will investigate the system with computational methods.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
MINBUBBLE: Mineral-Driven Bubble Nucleation for Critical Raw Materials Recovery in Flotation tackles fundamental scientific questions in how mineral particles can be better recovered. Sustainable access to critical raw materials is an environmental and geopolitical imperative, and current mineral extraction and refining methods are inadequate to meet these demands. Specifically, the recovery of minerals using froth flotation struggles to capture the finest fraction of particles due to insufficient attachment of particles to the bubbles. Worsening quality of ores also means that finer fractions are more commonly encountered in operations. 

To recover the fines, one solution may be to abruptly decrease the pressure of the system and initiate bubble formation directly on the mineral particle surfaces. This process is known as dissolved gas flotation (DGF), but it is not used in industrial mineral recovery due to a persistent lack of knowledge regarding the physicochemical processes that drive DGF. At NTNU, experimental work using microfluidics and a lab-scale flotation setup is planned to provide new data and understanding of the generation of bubbles in the presence of different minerals and varying water properties. Together, the experimental and computational results will establish the viability of DGF for extracting critical raw materials as a new, sustainable approach.

The project MINBUBBLE is led by Associate Professor Nadia Shardt in collaboration with Professor Gisle Øye at NTNU and Assistant Professor Shahab Mirjalili at KTH. It is funded under the call topic “Critical Raw Materials” by the Det Norske Veritas Foundation.

As part of the UNCHANGE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

About the project
About the UNCHANGE project  

UNCHANGE (UNderstanding change in Cultural HeritAge: the Next Generation of Experts) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network that brings together leading European universities, research institutions, and industry partners to train the next generation of heritage scientists. The project focuses on understanding, documenting, and monitoring change in cultural heritage using advanced technologies, including imaging, materials analysis, artificial intelligence, and data science. Through an interdisciplinary and international research environment, UNCHANGE equips doctoral candidates with the skills needed to address current and future challenges in cultural heritage conservation and preservation.

About the specific Doctoral projectObjectives: (1) Investigate novel object representations, such as Gaussians and Ray Fields, in measuring change for CH objects. (2) Investigate novel object representations in capturing and visualizing CH objects. The above objectives reflect current trends in the development of new object representations that are ‘AI-Friendly’, given the pervasiveness of AI methods in all types of processing.Expected results: Determination of the effect of machine learning-friendly object representations in capturing, visualizing and measuring change on CH objects.

NHH's Department of Finance is seeking to add faculty members with an internationally competitive research agenda. NHH offers the opportunity to participate in a program for university pedagogy, and candidates hired for tenure-track position as Assistant Professor or four-year position as Assistant Professor must take one basic module of the program during the fixed-term period. Candidates hired for the tenure-track position as Associate Professor, who cannot document at least 200 hours of pedagogical coursework at the time of promotion to a permanent position, must complete this program within two years.
 
NHH values effective communication and expects our faculty to have good language skills in both English and Norwegian. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level (The Common European Framework) within three years of appointment to a permanent position. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position as Associate Professor are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level within three years of appointment to the tenure-track position. Swedish and Danish are considered equivalent to Norwegian. NHH offers courses in Norwegian for employees who may not initially have Norwegian or another Scandinavian language proficiency.
NHH offers
We offer a seven-year tenure-track position, either as Assistant Professor or Associate Professor, depending on qualifications. As a successful tenure-track Associate Professor, NHH will grant a full professorship, all dependent on specific criteria. We also offer a four-year Assistant Professor position. Four-year Assistant Professor of Finance position will only be relevant for successful applicants who cannot be hired in a tenure-track position due to the regulations related to such positions. To be qualified for a tenure-track position, it should not be more than five years since the PhD degree was achieved (may be extended, for example in connection with statutory leaves). For candidates undertaking their PhD, the expected completion of the PhD thesis should be no later than the date of commencement in the position.

Salary is negotiable according to Norwegian State Salary Scale. All state employees will be members of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK), and receive good welfare benefits such as paid parental leave. External research grants and teaching in executive programs offer opportunities for supplementing this salary.

Female associate professors appointed to permanent academic positions may apply for research leave (sabbatical) with half the standard accrual period, in accordance with NHH’s applicable guidelines. This will apply for the first two years of research leave.

NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.

A maximum of 10 published or unpublished research papers (for the position as Associate Professor tenure-track) or a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers (for the position as Assistant Professor tenure-track or four-year Assistant Professor) should also be attached for evaluation. The application and enclosed documentation should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click 'Apply for this job'. For English version, go to the menu at the top right corner.
